ArtifactId.description: Which Pinned artifact: its kind, its name and its build.

ArtifactKind.description:
What a Pinned artifact is (ADR 0098: the clean-up's rule covers every
kind). An entry of a kind the engine does not know is one it cannot read,
and keeps.

oneOf.description: A browser build, such as Chrome for Testing's.
The versioned copy of an executable a Daemon runs from (ADR 0024).
The engine executable a Product's Rust crate downloads (ADR 0051).

Checkpoint.description:
A Checkpoint as the engine reports it (ADRs 0002, 0102 and 0116): a
consistent, self-contained copy of a Run's state, complete at its
location before it is reported, from which the Run resumes on this
machine or another one.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, in lowercase hexadecimal.

journal_position.description:
The position of the run's journal it holds: how many commits of the
run file it contains. A resume from it redoes the work after.

location.description: Where it is: the file's path on the engine's machine.

run_epoch.description:
The run epoch of the writer that took it (ADR 0003), which a
destination compares and sets: one older than it holds is refused.

Completeness.description:
Whether a Run's results cover everything in its scope (ADRs 0005 and
0029).

oneOf.description: It finished, but the engine cannot vouch that nothing was missed.

keys.description:
The keys to explain, each a key or a prefix of keys, such as
`timeout`; every key when empty.

origin.description:
Where those run values come from: a scope's `settings` option by
default, or the CLI's flags when the CLI asks a Daemon.

project.description: The project configuration to explain with.

settings.description:
Run-layer values to explain with, as a Run's `settings` would give
them.

ConsoleFailure.description:
Why a Daemon's Console did not start: an Error code, its message and
what to do instead.

ConsoleState.description:
Where a Daemon's Console is, as its runtime file and `daemon status`
report it.

oneOf.description: The Console is served at this URL, such as `http://127.0.0.1:7801/`.
The Console did not start; the Daemon still serves its Clients.
The engine carries no Console, as an SDK crate's linked engine.

DaemonEndpoint.description:
Where a Daemon or an Attached engine's private endpoint listens (ADR
0024): a `0600` Unix socket on macOS and Linux, loopback TCP on
Windows.

clients.description: How many Clients are connected, the caller and Consoles included.

console.description: Where its Console is served, or why it is not.

kept_alive.description:
Whether it never stops idle: `--keep-alive`, a held Schedule or an
installed service.

live_runs.description: How many of its Runs are live.

product.description: The Product the Daemon runs as.

DaemonStopping.description: What `daemon.stop` answers, before the Daemon stops.

live_runs.description: How many live Runs it stops, each resumable from its own state.

total_bytes.description: The bytes the answer announced, when it did.

product.description: The Product the engine runs as.

product_major.description: The major of its Product version, which names its per-major state.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the engine speaks.

after.description:
The position of the last event the Client read: the subscription
resumes after it, or starts with `events.resync` when the engine no
longer holds it. Absent, it starts with the next event.

ExplainedSetting.description: One setting as `config explain` shows it.

applied.description:
Whether this engine applies it: `false` for a key only the other
Product honours, which a shared file may hold (ADR 0087).

cap.description: An Operator policy's cap on it, if any.

locked_by.description:
The layer that locked it, if any: an Operator policy's lock, a
Recipe that declares it without exposing it, or the default for an
honesty guarantee.

origin.description: For the run layer, where the value came from.

products.description: The Products that honour it, from its Product mark (ADR 0095).

value.description:
The effective value, or for a key this engine does not apply, the
value its highest layer wrote.

weakens.description:
Whether its value weakens a guarantee class or switches off a costly
control, which the results it touches are marked with (ADR 0028).

GotoParams.description: What `page.goto` takes: the page, and the URL it goes to.

oneOf.description:
It ended early: by a Limit, an abort, its timeout, the loss of its
engine or exhausted resources.
An error in the engine or the program's code ended it.

Navigated.description:
What a navigation answers: the document's response, or none for a
navigation within the same document, to a URL no server answers, such as
`about:blank`, or back or forward from the last entry of the page's
history. A 404 or a 500 is a response, a value.

NewPageParams.description: What `run.new_page` takes: the Run whose default Session opens the page.

PageBodyParams.description: What `page.body` takes: the body to read.

run_id.description: The Run whose folder holds it.

PageBodyRead.description: What `page.body` answers once it sent the last chunk.

PageId.description: A page of a Run, named by the engine when it opens it.

PageOpened.description:
What `run.new_page` answers: the page, and the Session it belongs to,
which `page.session()` returns.

session_id.description: Its Session: the Run's default Session.

PageResponse.description: The response to a request of a page, such as a navigation's document.

headers.description: Its headers, their names lower-cased, as the browser received them.

PointInTime.description: A point in time in UTC, as RFC 3339.

Position.description: An event's position among every event of one engine, which only goes up.

Product.description:
One of Goodfetch's two Products (ADR 0084), by its mark as the catalog
writes it.

ProductVersion.description: A Product version, `major.minor.patch` with an optional pre-release (ADR 0090).

ProjectSettings.description:
A project configuration's values, which a Client reads where it runs and
sends with a scope it opens (ADR 0083).

path.description: The file's path, as the Client found it.

settings.description: Its settings, nested as the file nests them.

Resync.description:
What `events.resync` gives: the current state, from which the stream
continues.

runs.description: The axes of each Run the engine knows, live or ended.

RunAbortParams.description: What `run.abort` takes: the Run, and whether the abort was forwarded.

forwarded.description:
Set by an engine that forwards the abort to the owner the Run index
names (ADR 0031): an engine that does not own the Run then answers
`run_not_owned` instead of taking its writer role.

RunAxes.description:
A Run's three axes as they are now (ADR 0029): what
`run.axes_changed` reports, and what a resync gives of each Run.

completeness.description: Whether its results cover its scope, once it ended.

verdict.description: Whether its own checks prove what it committed, once it ended.

location.description:
Where to write the Checkpoint, a path on the engine's machine; by
default where the engine keeps the Run's Checkpoints, its own folder.

run_epoch.description: The run epoch the Checkpoint is taken under.

RunId.description: A Run ID (ADR 0036): lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, never a name Windows reserves for a device.

RunOrigin.description: Where a run-layer value came from (ADR 0083).

RunReport.description:
What a Run states about itself when it ends (ADR 0102): its three axes
(ADR 0029) and when it ran.

checkpoint.description:
The last Checkpoint written of it in this engine, when one was (ADR
0102).

completeness.description: Whether its results cover its scope.

policy_version.description:
The version of the Operator policy it ran under, when one applied
(ADR 0028).

stop_reason.description: Why it stopped, when it did.

verdict.description: Whether its own checks prove what it committed.

weakened_by.description:
Every setting it ran with that weakens a guarantee class or switches
off a costly control, with its value and layer (ADR 0028).

checkpoint.description:
A Checkpoint to resume from, a path on the engine's machine, which
becomes the Run's state in this engine's run folder; by default the
Run resumes from its run file on this machine.

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

settings.description:
The Run's settings from the resume on, nested by key: the run layer
(ADRs 0083 and 0102).

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

run_id.description:
The Run's ID; the engine generates a lowercase ULID when it is
absent. An existing ID returns that Run when the caller and the
inputs match, and fails with `run_conflict` otherwise.

settings.description: The Run's settings, nested by key: the run layer (ADR 0083).

RunStarted.description: What a start answers once its Run is started, never at its end.

needs.description:
The Product it needs (ADR 0098): Collie until it uses an entry the
catalog marks Foxhound's, Foxhound from then on.

key.description: The key to keep the value under.

SampleStorePutResult.description: What a sample store answers once it kept a value.

replaced.description: Whether a value was already kept under the key.

SessionId.description: A Session of a Run, named by the engine when it opens it.

SettingLimit.description:
A setting that decided an outcome: its key, its value and the layer that
set it (ADRs 0028 and 0079).

SettingsExplanation.description:
What `config.explain` answers and `config explain --json` prints:
every setting's effective value, the layer that set it and the layer
that locked it (ADR 0028), and the files read.

files.description: The files of the configuration layers, lowest first.

policy_version.description:
The Operator policy's version, `sha256:` and the first 16 hex digits
of its file's digest, which the run report names; `None` without a
policy.

settings.description: Each setting, by key.

SettingsFile.description: A layer's file, as `config explain` names it.

found.description: Whether it exists; a missing file sets nothing.

SettingsLayer.description: The layers settings resolve through, lowest first (ADRs 0028 and 0083).

oneOf.description:
The run: a program's settings, a call's argument, a CLI flag or an
Integration's form.

StartedAs.description: Whether a start began its Run or found it.

oneOf.description:
Its Run ID named a Run started before with the same inputs, which is
returned as it is.

It was interrupted and goes on from its committed state, its run
file or a Checkpoint, at the next run epoch (ADRs 0002, 0003 and
0102).

StopReason.description:
Why a Run stopped (ADR 0102); the other causes join with the tickets that
stop Runs for them.

oneOf.description:
Its program, a person or a Client aborted it, a Connection's close
included (ADR 0078).

It was paused: checkpointed and stopped, to be resumed by its Run ID
(RT-11).

It was migrated: checkpointed and stopped, to be resumed from its
Checkpoint on another machine (ADR 0002).

Its `timeout.run` passed, and it stopped at its next safe point,
resumable with a fresh clock (ADR 0080); no Error code of its own.

SubscriptionEnded.description:
What `events.subscribe` answers when its subscription ends without the
Client cancelling it: the engine stopped.

Tag.description: An opaque text a Run is tagged with (ADR 0036).

Tags.description: A Run's tags, in the order given.

Verdict.description: Whether a Run's own checks prove what it committed (ADR 0029).

oneOf.description:
Every check the Run relies on passed, none was switched off, and no
Effect is left uncertain.
Everything else: a person reviews it.

error_codes.description: The host has addresses only in an IP family the Session holds no local address of, such as IPv6 addresses for a Session bound to an IPv4 address. Add a local address of that family to the run's local addresses, or reach the host another way.
error_codes.name: address_family_unavailable

error_codes.description: A pinned download the call needed failed: the network, an HTTP status, or bytes whose digest is not the pinned one. Retry, or install beforehand with the Product's `browsers install`, or point `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` at a prepared cache.
error_codes.name: artifact_download_failed

error_codes.description: The `offline` setting refused a pinned download the call needed. Run the Product's `browsers install` beforehand where the cache is writable, point `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` at a prepared cache, or lift `offline` where it was set.
error_codes.name: artifact_unavailable_offline

error_codes.description: The Run's folder holds no body of this ID: the Run or the body is unknown, or the ID is not a body's.
error_codes.name: body_not_found

error_codes.description: The browser's build is installed, but it did not start or did not open the page: it exited, or its connection refused or fell silent. The details name its executable and how it ended.
error_codes.name: browser_launch_failed

error_codes.description: The browser build a launch needs is not in the Browser cache and the engine cannot write that cache, such as an image's read-only `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH`; or a browser named by channel or path is not there. Run the Product's `browsers install` where the cache is writable, install the browser of that channel, or correct the path.
error_codes.name: browser_not_installed

error_codes.description: The call was stopped in flight, at its next cancellation point: its Client sent `$/cancel`, or what it needed was closed under it.
error_codes.name: call_cancelled

error_codes.description: The call was made on a value its program had closed: a Connection, or a Run, Session or Page under it. A value never reopens: connect again, or start the Run again by its Run ID.
error_codes.name: closed

error_codes.description: The Console did not start: another program holds the port of `console.address`. The Daemon still serves its Clients. Stop the other program, or set `console.address` to a free port (port 0 takes any free one) and restart the Daemon.
error_codes.name: console_port_in_use

error_codes.description: The call's deadline passed before what it waited for came, such as a response's first byte or a navigation. Its `limit` names the timeout's setting, its value and the layer that set it: raise that setting, or wait for the right thing.
error_codes.name: deadline_exceeded

error_codes.description: The Attached engine ended before its Connection was closed, so the call has no answer. Its details carry the exit code or signal and the last 64 KiB of its stderr.
error_codes.name: engine_exited

error_codes.description: `connect()` found no engine executable to start: the Product's engine-path variable names no executable, or the Product's platform package is not installed. The `fix` names the variable or the package.
error_codes.name: engine_not_found

error_codes.description: The engine wrote a line that is not one JSON-RPC message on the Connection, such as a log line on an Attached engine's stdout, so the Client ended the Connection. A bug in Goodfetch: report it with the line its details carry.
error_codes.name: engine_output_invalid

error_codes.description: Windows refused to start the file: Smart App Control, or another App Control policy, blocks executables without a signature or reputation it trusts. Goodfetch never re-signs a file it did not build. For a browser, use the Goodfetch Chromium or an installed Chrome by channel; otherwise turn Smart App Control off, or ask the device's administrator to allow the file.
error_codes.name: executable_blocked_by_smart_app_control

error_codes.description: The bytes of a file could not be written: no space or quota left, or an I/O error, or any failure where the engine keeps its files. No partial file is left. Free space where the files go, or ask the Daemon's operator, then make the same call again.
error_codes.name: file_write_failed

error_codes.description: A file, such as a run state or a Checkpoint, is of a format version this engine cannot read: a newer minor or major, written by a newer engine, which `fix` says to upgrade to, or an older major, which `upgrade-files` upgrades. The file is left as it is.
error_codes.name: format_version_unsupported

error_codes.description: The engine's own resolver got no usable answer for the host name: its name servers timed out, refused the query, failed or could not be reached. Check the name servers of the system's resolver configuration, or map the name with the `resolve` setting.
error_codes.name: name_lookup_failed

error_codes.description: The resolver found no address for the host name. The engine's own resolver, used on Linux and for Sessions with a local address, reads the system's resolver configuration and hosts file but asks neither NSS modules (such as a directory service or a VPN client's) nor multicast DNS, so a name only they resolve, such as a `.local` name, fails here. Map such a name to its address with the `resolve` setting, or correct the name.
error_codes.name: name_not_resolved

error_codes.description: The navigation reached no document: the browser's network error, such as `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, is in the details, or the browser failed it for a reason it did not name.
error_codes.name: navigation_failed

error_codes.description: Another navigation of the page started before this one committed, so this one reached no document: the page went where the other took it.
error_codes.name: navigation_interrupted

error_codes.description: The call asks a Daemon about itself, and this engine is an Attached engine. Ask the Daemon of the major, found through its runtime file, or run `daemon status`.
error_codes.name: not_a_daemon

error_codes.description: The running engine's Product does not carry what was asked: a Client that needs Foxhound reached a Collie engine, or a call, a setting or a value only Foxhound carries reached one. Run it with Foxhound, which contains everything Collie does, or connect to a Foxhound engine.
error_codes.name: not_in_product

error_codes.description: The page's renderer crashed, or its browser process was lost while the call ran; `browser_exit` says how the browser ended when it is what was lost. The page is gone: open another.
error_codes.name: page_crashed

error_codes.description: The engine does not speak the protocol version the Client's `hello` names: it accepts its own major with the same or an older minor. Upgrade the older side.
error_codes.name: protocol_version_unsupported

error_codes.description: Another engine holds the Run's writer lock, and the owner the Run index names did not take the action: it did not answer, or does not own the Run. The engine retried the lock 5 times over about a second; the writer may end, so try again later.
error_codes.name: run_busy

error_codes.description: The Run ID names a Run started with other inputs, or by another caller; the details list each difference. Start under another Run ID.
error_codes.name: run_conflict

error_codes.description: The Run ID is not one the engine takes: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 128, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, never a name Windows reserves for a device.
error_codes.name: run_id_invalid

error_codes.description: Another engine holds the Run's writer lock, so this one cannot write the Run; the other may end.
error_codes.name: run_in_use

error_codes.description: No Run has this Run ID: the Run index does not list it.
error_codes.name: run_not_found

error_codes.description: The action was forwarded to this engine as the Run's owner, and this engine does not own the Run: the Run index named an engine that has since ended or restarted. The engine that forwarded it retries the Run's writer lock.
error_codes.name: run_not_owned

error_codes.description: The Run's state is missing, damaged or cannot be written at its location; the details give the path. The engine never starts afresh under that Run ID.
error_codes.name: run_state_unavailable

error_codes.description: The sample operation refused the text.
error_codes.name: sample_refused

error_codes.description: The Run is bound to the machine its Session source is on, and this is another machine: its login would reach sites from a new IP under the same cookies. Resume it on its own machine, or serve its Session source through a Browser host.
error_codes.name: session_bound_to_machine

error_codes.description: A value of the wrong type or out of the setting's own range, an empty or unparsable deployment variable, or a settings file that does not parse.
error_codes.name: setting_invalid

error_codes.description: A value a lower layer locked or capped, outside a Recipe's exposed bounds, or one only a lower layer may set or widen, such as `tls.trusted_cas` from a run. `limit` names the setting and the layer that holds it.
error_codes.name: setting_locked

error_codes.description: A setting given where it cannot take effect: in a layer that may not hold it, such as `browser_cache.max_unused_age` outside user configuration and an Operator policy, or on a Run it does not apply to, such as a crawl's setting on a Collie Run.
error_codes.name: setting_not_applicable

error_codes.description: A key no Product knows, or an unknown `GOODFETCH_` variable. The message names the closest valid one.
error_codes.name: setting_unknown

error_groups.description: The program is wrong: its call, its settings or its own handler code. Fix the program.
error_groups.name: program

error_groups.description: A policy, a Limit, a lock or a person refused. Change a setting, raise the Limit or ask the operator.
error_groups.name: refused

error_groups.description: The page or site never reached the state the call needed. Read the Run trace; change the step, the wait or the Access mode.
error_groups.name: page

error_groups.description: The Model provider's answer was unusable. Change the model or the strategy.
error_groups.name: model

error_groups.description: The deadline passed. Raise it, or wait for the right thing.
error_groups.name: deadline_exceeded

error_groups.description: Something Goodfetch depends on is unreachable or gone. Retry, or fix the setup.
error_groups.name: unavailable

error_groups.description: A bug in Goodfetch. Report it.
error_groups.name: internal

events.description: A Pinned artifact the call needs is downloading into the Browser cache: the bytes received so far, out of those announced.
events.name: browser_cache.download_progress

events.description: The engine no longer holds the position the subscription resumes after: the events since are gone, and this gives the current state, from which the stream continues.
events.name: events.resync

events.description: A Run is being aborted: it stops at its next safe point. Lossless.
events.name: run.aborting

events.description: A Run's Lifecycle, Verdict or Completeness changed: it started running, or it ended. Lossless: while a subscriber's queue is full, the Run waits.
events.name: run.axes_changed

events.description: A Checkpoint of a Run is being written: on `run.checkpoint`, a pause, a migration, a clean stop or the periodic `checkpoint.interval`. Lossless.
events.name: run.checkpointing

events.description: A Run is being migrated to another machine: it checkpoints, then stops. Lossless.
events.name: run.migrating

events.description: A Run is stopping at its next safe point, with its cause: an abort, a pause or a migration. Lossless.
events.name: run.stopping

hook_stages.description: Before the sample operation repeats a text.
hook_stages.name: sample_before_echo

operations.description: Shows each setting's effective value, the layer that set it and the layer that locked it, from the built-in defaults, the Operator policy, user configuration and the project configuration and run values given, and lists the keys only the other Product honours as that Product's.
operations.name: config.explain

operations.description: Says what the Daemon runs as, where it listens, how many Clients and live Runs it has, and when it stops idle.
operations.name: daemon.status

operations.description: Stops the Daemon once it answered: its live Runs stop, each resumable from its own state, and its runtime file and socket are removed.
operations.name: daemon.stop

operations.description: Says which Product the engine runs as, its Product version and major, and the protocol version it speaks.
operations.name: engine.info

operations.description: Subscribes to the engine's events. The call stays in flight, sending its events in `$/events` batches, never more than the credits granted with `$/credit`, until it is cancelled. A lossless event is never dropped: while the subscription's queue is full, its producer waits. A telemetry event is coalesced with the unsent one of the same kind and scope, and counts it as `dropped`. Given `after`, it resumes after that position, or starts with `events.resync` when the engine no longer holds it.
operations.name: events.subscribe

operations.description: Reads a page body by its handle, for a Client that cannot read the handle's file: sends the body in `$/chunk` notifications of at most 64 KiB, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, then answers its size.
operations.name: page.body

operations.description: Goes back one entry in the page's history and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response, or none when there is no entry to go back to. The back/forward cache is off, so the document always loads again (ADR 0121).
operations.name: page.go_back

operations.description: Goes forward one entry in the page's history and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response, or none when there is no entry to go forward to. The back/forward cache is off, so the document always loads again (ADR 0121).
operations.name: page.go_forward

operations.description: Navigates the page to a URL and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response: a 404 or a 500 is a response, a value. A navigation that reaches no document raises `navigation_failed`, and one another navigation supersedes before it committed `navigation_interrupted`.
operations.name: page.goto

operations.description: Loads the page's document again and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response: a 404 or a 500 is a response, a value. A navigation that reaches no document raises `navigation_failed`, and one another navigation supersedes before it committed `navigation_interrupted`.
operations.name: page.reload

operations.description: Stops a Run at its next safe point, `stopped` and `incomplete`: no attempt in flight commits, and its work items return to pending. Answers its Run report; an ended Run's report is answered as it is. A Run whose engine died is stopped by this engine, which takes its writer role at the next run epoch; a Run another engine writes is stopped by that engine, the owner the Run index names.
operations.name: run.abort

operations.description: Writes a Checkpoint of a live Run now, through SQLite's online backup, where `location` says or where the engine keeps the Run's Checkpoints, and answers it once its file is complete, with its size, digest, run epoch and journal position. A Checkpoint the engine cannot write fails with `file_write_failed` and leaves no file.
operations.name: run.checkpoint

operations.description: Lets a Run finish and answers its Run report: a Run its program drives ends at once, `finished` and `complete`; a crawl ends once its work items are done. Cancelling the call ends only the wait.
operations.name: run.finish

operations.description: Migrates a live Run: checkpoints it where `location` says or where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, then stops it at its next safe point, `stopped` with the stop reason `migrate`, to be resumed from that Checkpoint on another machine. Answers its Run report, which names the Checkpoint.
operations.name: run.migrate

operations.description: Opens a page in the Run's default Session, which the first call opens with the Run's settings and every later call shares; `page.session()` reaches it. The first page launches the Run's browser, so a missing browser build raises its code from this call.
operations.name: run.new_page

operations.description: Pauses a live Run: checkpoints it, then stops it at its next safe point, `stopped` with the stop reason `pause` and resumable by its Run ID with `run.resume`, after a restart too. Answers its Run report, which names the Checkpoint.
operations.name: run.pause

operations.description: Resumes an interrupted Run from its committed state, its run file on this machine or the Checkpoint `checkpoint` names: it takes the Run's writer lock and the next run epoch, so every write of an earlier writer is refused, and redoes the work since that state; its recorded Clean-up rules digest is kept. A live Run is answered as it is, `existing`; a finished one as it is. A Run bound to another machine fails with `session_bound_to_machine`, and a Checkpoint of a format version this engine cannot read with `format_version_unsupported`.
operations.name: run.resume

operations.description: Starts a Run its program drives, and answers once it is started. A Run ID names the Run for good: a start with an existing Run ID returns that Run as it is when the caller and the inputs match, and fails with `run_conflict` otherwise.
operations.name: run.start

deprecated.note: A sample entry, which the real catalog replaces.

operations.description: Repeats a text back to the caller.
operations.name: sample.echo

plugin_kinds.description: Keeps values by key for the sample operations.

methods.description: Keeps a value under a key.
methods.name: put

plugin_kinds.name: sample_store

settings.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset, and a run already going takes a tightened cap at its next admission.
settings.name: admission.max_requests_per_minute

settings.description: How long a Pinned artifact no installed executable pins stays in the Browser cache unused before the clean-up deletes it, and how long an executable's entry counts as installed after it was last seen: 30 days. `null` turns the automatic clean-up off. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: browser_cache.max_unused_age

settings.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.
settings.name: checkpoint.interval

settings.description: The domains whose consent prompts a run accepts instead of refusing. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.
settings.name: consent.domains

settings.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7800 plus the major (7700 plus the minor during `0.y` previews), so each major's Console has its own port. Port 0 takes a free port, which the Daemon's runtime file and `daemon status` report. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.address

settings.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client, a visible Console tab included, waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: daemon.idle_timeout

settings.description: Whether the engine opens no connection nobody configured: every pinned download, such as a Pinned artifact missing from the Browser cache, fails with `artifact_unavailable_offline` before it connects, naming the command that supplies it beforehand. `false` by default; set at every layer, and an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: egress.offline

settings.description: Extra Filter lists, by URL or path. Their scriptlets run only when the value comes from an Operator policy or user or project configuration; from a Recipe or a run, only their blocking rules apply.
settings.name: filter_lists.extra

settings.description: Host names mapped to addresses before any lookup, in the engine's resolver and in Chromium, each address still checked by ADR 0017's resolved-address rule. Empty by default; an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: network.resolve

settings.description: How a Run shares Politeness with the other runs of its user: `shared` with every engine of the user (through the Politeness store when one is configured, else on the machine), `per_daemon` on the machine only, ignoring a store, or `run` for Politeness of its own. Anything but `shared` is listed in the Run's result.
settings.name: politeness.sharing

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.
settings.name: resolver.attempt_delay

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.
settings.name: resolver.resolution_delay

settings.description: The folder that holds the run folders, each named by its Run ID; by default the per-user, per-major data folder of the Goodfetch home.
settings.name: run_state.location

settings.description: How many times the sample operation repeats a text.
settings.name: sample.echo_repeats

settings.description: Secrets are given by Secret reference, never as values, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
settings.name: secrets.by_reference

settings.description: Where a Session's login comes from. A Recipe never sets or locks it; it may only expose it to its users.
settings.name: session.source

settings.description: How long a request may wait for its response's first byte before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.first_byte

settings.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.
settings.name: timeout.navigation

settings.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.
settings.name: timeout.run

settings.description: Domains whose certificate may fail verification, each with a pin, `any`, or `null` for trust on first use. A pin and `any` are taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration; a Recipe or a run may list a domain only for trust on first use.
settings.name: tls.accept_invalid_certs

settings.description: Extra certificate authorities by domain: certificate files or Secret references. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration, never from a Recipe or a run.
settings.name: tls.trusted_cas

settings.description: The domains whose Walls no run reads past, whatever another layer allows. Set only in an Operator policy.
settings.name: wall.denied_domains

settings.description: The domains whose Walls a run may read past by generic means. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.
settings.name: wall.domains

settings.description: The domains on which reading past a Wall may fetch a page again. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration, never by an answer.
settings.name: wall.refetch_domains

settings.description: Every webhook Goodfetch sends is signed, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
settings.name: webhook.signing

shared_type_values.description: A page that asks a person to prove they are human.
shared_type_values.name: captcha

shared_type_values.description: A page that checks the browser before it lets it through.
shared_type_values.name: challenge

shared_type_values.description: A wall that asks for consent before it shows the page (ADR 0048).
shared_type_values.name: consent_required

shared_type_values.description: The site refused the address the request came from.
shared_type_values.name: ip_block

shared_type_values.description: The site asked to be paid for the page (ADR 0045).
shared_type_values.name: payment_required

shared_type_values.description: The site refused because too many requests came too fast.
shared_type_values.name: rate_limit
